subtitles.en: Mike Wilson of Morgan Stanley writing several clearing events play out over the next few weeks.
subtitles.zh: 摩根士丹利的Mike Wilson写道，未来几周将有几项出清事件上演。

subtitles.en: This should provide attractive buying opportunities as the market looks ahead to another leg higher in earnings growth. Mike joins us now for more. Mike, good morning.
subtitles.zh: 这应会提供有吸引力的买入机会，因市场预期盈利增长将再上一个台阶。Mike现在加入我们带来更多分析。Mike，早上好。

subtitles.en: Good morning. Those clearing events were the feature of your note to start this week. You identified three of them. Can you share them with us this morning?
subtitles.zh: 早上好。这些出清事件是你本周初报告的重点。你指出了三个。今天能和我们分享一下吗？

subtitles.en: Yeah. Well, first of all, maybe we get 12% bond in Brazil too. Don't forget about that.
subtitles.zh: 好的。首先，也许我们在巴西还能获得12%的债券收益。别忘了这一点。

subtitles.en: So, what I would say is, you know, the markets have a way, and part of the reason why the people are kind of looking at pastles. There's so much going on, they can't focus.
subtitles.zh: 所以，我想说的是，市场有其运行方式，人们关注过去的部分原因是事情太多，无法集中注意力。

subtitles.en: So, the markets kind of grab onto what they know, which is earnings are still pretty good.
subtitles.zh: 因此，市场会抓住它们所知道的，即盈利仍然相当不错。

subtitles.en: Rates have actually come down, it's been more steady, so that's not a bad environment to be looking to add risk. Now, the three things that we were most focused on now,
subtitles.zh: 利率实际上已经下降，更加稳定，所以这不是一个糟糕的环境来考虑增加风险。现在，我们最关注的三个事情，

subtitles.en: and in no particular order, the obvious ones are the midterm elections, which is always a clearing event. I mean, historically, it's always a good time to be adding risk into that event. Now,
subtitles.zh: 不分先后，明显的是中期选举，这总是一个出清事件。我的意思是，历史上，这总是增加风险的好时机。现在，

subtitles.en: sometimes it could linger another month or so, but over the next six to 12 months, 100% certainty going back to 1952, you make positive returns, and usually double digits.
subtitles.zh: 有时可能会再持续一个月左右，但在未来6到12个月，100%确定，回溯到1952年，你会获得正回报，通常还是两位数。

subtitles.en: So, that's just something to keep in the back of your mind, as things get wobbly, keep that in the back of your mind as you should be stepping in and adding risk.
subtitles.zh: 所以，这只是你要记在心里的事情，当事情变得波动时，记住这一点，你应该介入并增加风险。
en_highlights: keep that in the back of your mind

subtitles.en: Number two, I think, is around this idea around AI catbacks and the scarcity of capital.
subtitles.zh: 第二点，我认为是关于AI资本回流和资金稀缺性的观点。

subtitles.en: Okay, that one's pretty well understood too, and I think these companies are dealing with it properly, right? So, they're doing the back and forth between equity issuance and debt issuance.
subtitles.zh: 这一点也相当好理解，我认为这些公司处理得当，对吧？他们在股权发行和债务发行之间来回操作。

clip_research.source_claim: Wilson says that over the next six to 12 months after midterm elections, going back to 1952, there is 100% certainty of positive returns, usually double digits.
clip_research.public_baseline: Multiple public sources (J.P. Morgan Asset Management, Yahoo Finance/Baird, simianx.ai) state the S&P 500 has risen in the 12 months after every midterm election since 1950, averaging roughly 15%.
clip_research.surprise_gap: Wilson's '100% certainty' framing is rhetorically strong but broadly consistent with the historical record cited publicly; the surprise is the absolutist phrasing rather than a factual contradiction.

evidence.fact: Wilson identifies midterm elections as a clearing event and claims 100% certainty of positive 6-12 month returns since 1952, usually double digits.

evidence.fact: Bloomberg (Nov 2022): Wilson urged investors to stay bullish ahead of midterms, calling them a clearing event.

forbidden_claims: Do not claim Wilson predicted a specific percentage gain or named all three clearing events if the transcript does not.
Do not claim Wilson's historical claim is false; public data broadly supports positive post-midterm returns.

Do not claim Wilson changed his position without exact prior statements.

notes: Chinese display forms for Mike Wilson are inferred from standard financial-media usage; the retrieved snippets are English-only, so entity confidence is capped at medium.

data_driven_lessons.source: KC桌面-视频号动态数据明细.csv, 114 rows, July 2026 local analysis
winning_patterns: 机构/人物权威 + 具体数字/资产 + 强问题，例如 高盛王逸：4-5万亿城市更新会拖住楼市吗
大机构/名人 + 被逼/陷阱/真相/转向 等张力词，例如 野村辜朝明：日本央行被逼到墙角
具体数据 + 政策动作疑问，例如 6月PMI释放积极信号，政府会加码吗
反常识判断 + 下一步条件，例如 低估值可能是价值陷阱，需等待政策转向消费
中国相关议题更容易获得点击，但表达要落在政策、需求、信心、估值、产业升级这些正向框架
外资或海外权威给出对中国更积极的判断时，反差本身就是主标题，不要埋在摘要里
让观众产生单一强反应：居然如此、终于有人说、他说的是真的吗、原来中国优势在这里
大实话角度来自表达者身份与观点反差；言行反差角度必须有公开动作或披露支撑
涉及中国比较优势时，优先把外国企业被迫调整、海外权威改口或中国优势被低估写成冲突
avoid_patterns: 过长的新闻句，尤其是 24 字以上还塞多个从句
只有 策略/机会/影响/前瞻/市场/风险 这类泛词，没有具体对象或张力
美国宏观泛标题如果没有美联储/鲍威尔等强锚点，点击明显弱
纯描述式标题，例如 某市场短期风险与长期催化剂，缺少问题和冲突
经济危机/金融危机/崩盘/崩溃 这类过硬负面财经词
把事实换成疑问号但没有反差，例如 回报路径在哪、未来如何、能否实现
陌生英文人名或机构全称占据第一行，却没有告诉观众这个人为什么值得听
把 Bloomberg LP 等来源或公司法律后缀误当成采访对象
没有公开证据却暗示嘉宾撒谎、操纵或言行不一
